newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia finance companies bad debt declines.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia finance companies bad debt declines.

text.p: The bad debt portfolio of Malaysian finance companies improved in the first half of the current year, Bank Negara said on Wednesday.

It said in a statement after the central bank's annual meeting with chief executives of finance companies that non-performing loans fell to 6.4 percent of total loans at end-June against 6.8 percent at the end of December, 1995.
The industry's deposits in the first half rose by 10.2 billion ringgit to 80.2 billion, the statement said.
Loans extended by finance companies in the same period rose by 8.1 billion ringgit to 72.8 billion.
The central bank said of the expansion in credit from finance companies the largest share of 36.1 percent was to the consumption sector followed by property sector with a share of 27.6 percent.
In the first half, the pre-tax profit of all finance companies was 768 million ringgit against 728 million in the corresponding period of last year, the statement said.
